Definition: properly, curative, i.e. literally (concretely) a medicine, or (abstractly) a cure; figuratively (concretely) deliverance, or (abstractly) placidity
BiblicalUsage: marpêʼ is a cure, a medicine, and sometimes the health itself. In Jeremiah 8:15 the people look for peace and for a time of health, and behold trouble, and in 2 Chronicles 36:16 the wrath of the LORD arises until there is no remedy. In 2 Chronicles 21:18 Jehoram is smitten with an incurable disease, and in Ecclesiastes 10:4 yielding pacifies great offences. The word is the healing that comes and the healing that is refused.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe marpêʼ teaches me that God is the healer. I hold that when there is no remedy, it is because the wound has been refused, not because He cannot heal.
